requirements.text: Identify the Response Category (1 or 2), your understanding of scope and objectives, and summarize approach, proposed staff and estimated duration.
Describe at least three similar, successful projects with start/end dates, staff count, your role, business need, target audience and approximate users, technical solution, and final results.
Provide a client reference for each project (organization, name and title, project role, phone, email); references must agree to be contacted.
Describe how the architecture supports load balancing and workload distribution; attach a reference architecture covering hosting environment and application architecture.

Describe how the solution tracks: availability, response times, web/application/OS processes, database queries and I/O, throughput, CPU/memory/network/database utilization, active users, error rates, garbage collection.
Describe how new monitoring parameters are added.
Describe how performance degradation is detected and reported.
Detail the logging and error-tracking process, including the list of items logged and tracked.
Describe high availability and scalability through dynamic allocation of processing power, memory, database capacity, network bandwidth and application server capacity.
Describe the security model for the hosting infrastructure and the application.
Describe safeguards that prevent users from inadvertently impairing system performance.
Detail the approach to comprehensive database monitoring.
Describe the process for guaranteeing database consistency.
Describe the disaster recovery options included.
List the environments included in the solution.
Describe the process for problem identification, root cause determination and resolution.
99.9% of the time, at least 2,500 concurrent users must have consistent access to logins and user functions without timeouts or instability; describe how the solution provides this.

Demonstrate scalability: when CPU, memory, database performance or other essential resources cross critical thresholds, provision resources to prevent or recover from degradation; describe the approach.

Provide real-time monitoring of key performance metrics (agreed with MOCS), visible to MOCS staff; for each application metric give name, description, impact, acceptable range and reporting frequency.

subsections.title: 2.3 Functional Requirements
subsections.note: Category 2 proposers only; fuller descriptions are in Appendix F of the RFS (not yet captured).

requirements.text: Self-service capture of vendor indicative, background and performance information; vendor/principal disclosure, caution and performance evaluation.
Manage Pre-Qualified Lists tied to a managing agency; citywide or agency-only flags.
Manage vendor responsibility determinations, including required City and external reporting.
Vendor document vault: upload specified document types and pull them into proposals, contracts, invoices, disclosures and PQL applications.
Vendor budget management: certification of funds, invoice and payment tracking, advances and recoupments.
Subcontractor management: submission and approval, subcontract modifications, payments to subcontractors.
Let vendors and agencies monitor progress toward M/WBE goals per contract.
Import goods catalogs from master agreement contracts; catalog items viewable citywide for requisitions.
Internal business and financial approvals of goods requisitions before encumbrance; vendor order module with estimated delivery dates.
Receipts confirming delivery; vendor invoices matched against order and receipt, with agency review before FMS disbursement.
Contract requisition, solicitation, creation and management.
Organize requisitions and sourcing projects into programs by citywide initiative.
Request direct orders or task orders, or start a new sourcing event or contract action.
Pre-solicitation review: market assessment, cost estimate, selection of procurement method.
Draft and publish solicitations to selected vendors in accordance with PPB rules.
Evaluate responses per PPB rules, including multiple rounds/addenda, open-ended solicitations and real-time bidding.
Link responsibility determination to selected vendor; create and route recommendation for award.
Draft contracts with collaborative City–vendor editing; execution, oversight review, public hearings, certification of funds, Comptroller registration package.
Contract amendment and change order management.
Register and manage Master Agreements (MA1, MMA1, MAR) including modifications and task-order rotation models.
Agency management of certification of funds, encumbrances and accounting lines across requisition, contract, amendment, order and invoice.
Budget and encumbrance validation, submission, and oversight approval workflows.
Invoicing and receiving for direct orders, contracts and task orders, integrated with the City financial management system.
Vendor submission of contract budgets for contracts and purchase orders.
Manage retainage terms on contract budgets and related invoices.
Flexible pricing and blanket orders for specialized purchases (e.g. fuel, bulk supply).
Real- or near-real-time order, invoice and disbursement integrations with the City financial system.
Support capital, expense and mixed funding structures across modules.
Payment advances and recoupment.
Integrations with City authentication, financial and budget systems (OTI, FISA, OMB) using standard protocols (API, FTP, LDAP) with security and management tooling.
Programmatic and user read access to all application data via SQL-like queries, exportable to Excel, CSV, XML.
Document vault for vendor, agency and admin users; sharing rules (shared docs can't be archived/deleted; read-only viewing).
Agencies set document submission requirements per step; link documents from device or vault; some converted to PDF.
Configure and design PASSPort global pages.
Map user profiles and authorizations to homepage features.
MOCS Admin management of agency approval rules, routing and delegation by dollar thresholds.
Configure and generate E-PINs; search objects by partial or full E-PIN.
Generate PDFs from templates pulling Contract Object fields, with naming convention, into the agency vault.
Configure which objects use the document vault vs. attachments, and allowed document types.
State your understanding of the project objectives and goals.
Describe the approach and methodology (e.g. prototyping, RAD, Agile, COTS).
Project scope: contractor needs, proposed acceptance criteria and process, interaction with City staff and other contractors, and tasks by phase with resources, durations and milestones.

List deliverables (e.g. work plan, design document with security approach, test plan/scripts/results, production application, technical docs, deployment and back-out plans, transition plan, weekly status reports).
Category 1: initial phase expected within 8 months (setup → design → test env → test system → evaluation criteria → production by months 6–8); later phases within the following 12 months.
Category 2: sandbox, gap analysis and business process re-engineering within 8 months; full implementation, integration and migration within the following 18 months.
Phase 1 must be priced separately from all future phases (Categories 1 and 2).
Explicitly list scope exclusions; generic exclusions are not acceptable.
Describe reports: title, form and content, frequency.
List assumptions (assumptions conflicting with the Agreement are void).

Category 1 key roles: Project Manager*, Technical Project Lead*, Lead Infrastructure Architect*, Sr. Application Solution Engineer*, Senior Database Engineer*, Senior Implementation Engineer*, plus Implementation Engineer(s), with labor category and hourly rate; mark subcontractors.
Category 2 adds: Business Analyst Lead*, QA Lead*, Business Analysts, QA Analysts, BPR Lead, Change Management Lead.
Resume and at least one client reference per resource; for cloud or new-software work, resumes must show at least five years in the targeted environment.
Specify prevailing-wage mark-up, non-U.S. labor discounted rates, and specialized subcontractor cost-plus rates where applicable.
Organization chart and narrative showing interaction with City staff and other entities.
Describe the governance structure.
Fixed-price, deliverables-based structure showing hours and hourly rates per deliverable (alternatives such as T&M may be added).
Complete Attachment E – Price Proposal Worksheet (Staffing Plan, Total Charges, Phase 1 tabs) across all phases for up to six years.
Software/subscription and hardware costs with licensing structure and mark-ups (not above Attachment PRC; 0% on maintenance); prices at or below the lesser of contractor discount, NYS OGS or GSA.
Post-implementation support and maintenance annual fees, no overlap with acceptance and warranty; 0% mark-up.
Optional performance outcome measures and financial incentives/disincentives.
Payment schedule (monthly or by deliverable).
Warranty period for products and system deliverables of at least 12 months.

submissionChecklist.item: Proposal following Attachment A section order (Executive Summary, sections 1–5, Warranty)
Resumes and client references for every proposed resource
Attachment E – Price Proposal Worksheet, Phase 1 priced separately
M/WBE Utilization Plan meeting the 30% participation goal (or waiver request)
Submit in PASSPort before the due date
